quote: You guys were testing me on a number, and I'll ask you if it's still a good number.
stewart_read: Customer references a prior Ion touchpoint verifying a number with him, implying this may be a recycled or repeat-contact lead rather than a cold paid lead. The rep does not probe what that prior test was or when it happened.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have already known this was a recycled lead from internal notes and saw no need to re-ask, making the omission reasonable rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to spend 5 seconds confirming lead history ("when did we last talk?") — this changes how much bill-collection effort is actually required and whether data may already be on file.

quote: And then you can see where the the the south facing roof is wide open, including the garage roof is 90% open.
stewart_read: Customer is proactively describing excellent roof orientation and openness on both the house and a large detached garage — a strong qualification signal beyond what the standard roof_type_age question would surface.
coaching_implication: Rep validated this well ("looks great... full sun exposure") — the manager should note this as a model moment for how to receive an enthusiasm signal, and could coach the rep to explicitly log the garage roof as an expansion opportunity for the design team, not just verbally acknowledge it.

quote: But they built a giant solar field two miles south of my house here. And ever since that went online, my electric skyrocketed.
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a ready-made utility-grievance narrative — his bill spiked after a utility-scale solar field went online near him, which he frames with suspicion ("I hate to say this because I'm not trying to be negative"). This is a natural flip point: the rep could reinforce that his own solar would put him back in control instead of paying a utility that profits either way.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep's response ("That's super weird... that's way too much to power your house, so we can help for sure") does move toward the program pitch immediately after, so this could be read as an implicit flip rather than a miss.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to explicitly name the contrast next time: tie the customer's own words about the utility's solar field back to "that's exactly why owning your own system means your rate doesn't move when theirs does" — makes the inversion concrete instead of generic enthusiasm.

quote: I'm a disabled vet, and I've had 31 surgeries reconstructing me over the last twenty some years.
stewart_read: Rep responds warmly and thanks him for his service, which the customer receives well and keeps talking — this is a partial credit moment, not a full miss, since engagement continued and warmed further.
alternative_hypothesis: A stronger read is that this is adequate handling, not a miss — the customer's own follow-up ("I smile every day") suggests the rep's response landed fine even without an explicit value-bridge to solar.
coaching_implication: Acknowledge the rep handled this acceptably. For polish, coach a light bridge line after the thanks — something like reflecting that a stable, lower bill is one less thing to manage — without turning the moment transactional.

quote: And I just I don't like sitting around even even hell, my jaw was replaced two weeks ago, and I'm supposed to be off work for six weeks, and I went back to work yesterday.
stewart_read: A second, distinct vulnerability disclosure — customer went back to work against medical advice just two weeks after major surgery. Rep's response is limited to surprise ("Oh my gosh... at least you enjoy it") with no acknowledgment of the risk he's describing or bridge to how solar reduces one more thing he has to manage while overextended.
alternative_hypothesis: Because this follows immediately after the vet disclosure and the customer is clearly in a talkative, self-driven mode, the rep may have reasonably chosen not to slow the call further with a second heavy acknowledgment — over-dwelling could have felt performative.
coaching_implication: Flag as a pattern: two vulnerability disclosures in under two minutes, neither bridged to value. Coach the rep on a single crisp bridge line usable for either disclosure type so it doesn't require in-the-moment invention.

quote: K. Go ahead. Take a screenshot of that and then text that over to me if possible.
stewart_read: This marks the start of the actual bill-collection exchange (distinct from the earlier 00:16-06:04 property-app struggle). The customer works through a log-in wall at 14:13 before successfully sending the bill screenshot around 15:03 — several minutes of friction the rep waits out rather than pivoting to a verbal read-back per bill_collection.alternative_paths.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer was already narrating bill numbers aloud unprompted ("the actual electricity was $529... I used 5,300 kilowatt hours in February"), so the rep may have judged that a verbal pivot was unnecessary since usable numbers were already coming through verbally alongside the screenshot attempt.
coaching_implication: Coach rep to recognize when a customer is already giving usable numbers verbally and to capture those explicitly as backup rather than waiting purely on the photo/screenshot to land.

quote: Let's, shoot for Monday because today is my daughter's birthday, and she got a lot going on today and tomorrow.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a personal scheduling constraint; rep adapts smoothly and reschedules without friction, landing a concrete day/time.
coaching_implication: No coaching action needed here — flagged as an example of smooth, low-friction rescheduling the rep should recognize as a strength to repeat.
